- What the check counts: the read tool, bash `cat`/`sed`/`head` with a literal path, codemode nested reads. Not counted: loops, `$VAR` paths, `grep`/`awk`, a skill's text arriving in a brief.
- Send-backs since 2026-11-20: 10 tickets, 17 skill items. 12 true misses. 5 FALSE: #1199 (tdd and python) from a parsing bug: shlex treats a mid-word `#` (as in `spec#anchor`) as a comment, so every read after it on that command line is lost; #1134, #1136, #1137 ("python.") from a Skills: line ending in a period.
- False passes: 0 in 59 sessions.
- "codebase-design read in 4 of 119 sessions" (#644): reproduced exactly over all 119. It stands.

So the check is sound in direction and wrong in two concrete ways. Fix: lex without comments; strip trailing punctuation from Skills: names; answer "cannot tell" (exit 2, never a send-back) when a session names the SKILL.md in a call the reader cannot resolve. Counting more kinds of read is not needed.
